Xabi Alonso talks to Sky. “We want to show a good reaction from the last game … the proper fundamentals to compete … it is not just the defenders, it is the whole team … we are expecting an intense game … good atmosphere … we need to show we can compete at this level … today we need strong characters … big personalities … players on the bench ready to have a good impact … the game will be close … tight … we need to be aware of the small details … the next game is the best opportunity and we approach in that way today.”

Fri 27 Nov 2026 14.41 EST
First published on Fri 27 Nov 2026 13.30 EST
A cheery Oliver Glasner speaks to Sky Sports. “I always felt the backing of the owner … we have constant talks … always in direct contact … assessing what’s going well and not going well … discussing how we improve things … we are very honest … we are not pleased with the season so far … we wanted to have more points … the running standard will increase … the players are working hard during the week … we are competitive in the running … it needs a good structure … it is possible to beat Chelsea, like Leeds have shown last week … it is the first opportunity [Igor Jesus and Liam Delap] play together … both have different strengths … we need to score more goals, that is clear … nine goals from 11 rounds is not satisfying.”
Here’s how the Premier League table looks as we all barrel towards one-third-of-the-season territory. Chelsea can go fifth with a win tonight, and would be guaranteed to stay there for at least 19 hours, by which point we’ll know the fate of Brentford at Manchester United, and the outcome of the Leeds-Coventry 1987 FA Cup semi-final rematch). Nottingham Forest can rise as high as 14th with victory, but their rubber-stamped 19-hour stay will only extend if Leeds beat Coventry, in which case they’re guaranteed another two-and-a-half hours, after which all would be dependent on Ipswich’s result against Aston Villa. I’ll level with you, I’m killing time until kick-off.
Jamie Carragher and Toby Alderweireld eviscerated Chelsea’s defence earlier this week on Monday Night Football. Xabi Alonso seems to have taken that criticism seriously, because by the looks of it, he’s dropped Levi Colwill and replaced him in the centre of defence by Moisés Caicedo, with Jordan Henderson deputising for the Ecuadorian in midfield. That’s a ballsy call, given that Chelsea’s midfield crumbled to a premium grade of dust when Caicedo was injured against Leeds. At least he’ll still be on the pitch this time.
Chelsea make three changes to their starting team, in the wake of that 1-4 home skelping by Leeds. Jordan Henderson, Danny Welbeck and Pedro Neto are in; Levi Colwill, Emmanuel Emegha and Estêvão drop to the bench.
Forest make two changes to their starting XI following their 2-0 defeat at Bournemouth last weekend. Igor Jesus and Xaver Schlager replace Dan Ndoye and captain Ryan Yates, who both drop to the bench.
The teams
Nottingham Forest: Sels, Jair Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo, Munoz, McAtee, Schlager, Williams, Igor Jesus, Gibbs-White, Delap.
Subs: John Victor, Diomande, Sangare, Hudson-Odoi, Wood, Ndoye, Kalimuendo, Yates, Netz.
Chelsea: Martinez, Acheampong, Fofana, Lavia, Chavarria, Henderson, Caicedo, Pedro Neto, Palmer, Rogers, Welbeck.
Subs: Penders, Palestra, Barco, Colwill, Emegha, Quenda, Gusto, Nicoll-Jazuli, Estevao.
Referee: Andrew Madley
VAR: Lewis Smith
Preamble
Since returning to the Premier League in 2022, Nottingham Forest have yet to win this particular fixture. They’ve lost it three out of four times, though, the most recent defeat a 3-0 shellacking last October that got Ange Postecoglou the sack 15 minutes after the final whistle. Nobody’s expecting Oliver Glasner to get the old heave-ho should Forest extend their miserable record tonight, but with the Tricky Trees currently above the relegation places only thanks to goal difference, the Austrian could do with three precious points and a little time and space.
But it’s his opposite number Xabi Alonso who is under the real pressure tonight. Chelsea are eighth in the table and could go fifth tonight, a scenario that usually doesn’t merit the sounding of the crisis klaxon. But they were hammered 4-1 at home by big rivals Leeds last weekend, their second Premier League defeat in a row and their third in four matches. The defence is in tatters, the midfield falls apart when Moisés Caicedo isn’t there, the style of play is yet to be determined, and the boss used to play for Liverpool. Another defeat would set the cat, if not among the pigeons, then a couple of paces behind them, quietly waiting for the most effective moment to pounce.
The good news for Chelsea: that aforementioned record at the City Ground. The good news for Forest: they’ve already beaten Manchester City at home, and won at Stamford Bridge back in May. So good luck confidently predicting this. Kick-off is at 8pm GMT. It’s on!

נוטינגהאם פורסט וצ'לסי מתכוננות למפגש מסקרן בפרמייר ליג באצטדיון הסיטי גראונד. צ'לסי מגיעה לאחר תבוסה ביתית 1-4 מול לידס, תוצאה שהפעילה לחץ על המאמן צ'אבי אלונסו וגרמה לו לבצע שינויים בהגנה ובקישור. מנגד, נוטינגהאם פורסט מציגה סגל מעודכן שבו נכללים שחקנים כמו איגור ז'ז'וס וקסוור שלאגר.

בטבלת הפרמייר ליג, צ'לסי שואפת לטפס למקום החמישי בטבלה, בעוד נוטינגהאם פורסט נאבקת על מקומה ורוצה להתרחק מאזור הסכנה בתחתית. המפגש הקודם בין השניים במגרש זה זכור היטב, וההיסטוריה מראה כי הקבוצות מספקות משחקים צמודים וטעונים.
